record.original_question: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A 3-NU polymorphism phi : H^3 -> H satisfies phi(x, x, y) = phi(x, y, x) = phi(y, x, x) = x, and a polymorphism of S_H is called semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists. Is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if it has a semi-conservative 3-NU polymorphism?

evidence.quote: Let H be a br-graph, and S be the set {0, 1}. The switching graph SH of H is the br-graph on the set V(H) x S.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A br-graph is a graph H equipped with a distinguished partition of its edge set (so each edge carries a "type"); homomorphisms between br-graphs must respect both adjacency and edge type. For a br-graph H, let S = {0,1} and define the switching graph S_H to be the br-graph whose vertex set is V(H) × S, with edges defined so that the involution (v,0) ↔ (v,1) corresponds to "switching" at v. A polymorphism of a br-graph G of arity k is a homomorphism φ : G^k → G (where G^k is the categorical k-th power in the category of br-graphs). 

A polymorphism φ : G^k → G is called a weak near unanimity (WNU) polymorphism if it is idempotent (φ(x,…,x) = x) and satisfies
   φ(y,x,x,…,x) = φ(x,y,x,…,x) = ⋯ = φ(x,x,…,x,y)
for all x, y ∈ V(G). A ternary polymorphism φ : G^3 → G is called a 3-NU (near unanimity) polymorphism if
   φ(x,x,y) = φ(x,y,x) = φ(y,x,x) = x
for all x, y ∈ V(G).

A symmetric list on V(H) × S is an assignment L : V(H) × S → 2^{V(H) × S} such that (v,i) ∈ L(u,j) ⇔ (u,j) ∈ L(v,i). A polymorphism of S_H is called semi-conservative if, for every choice of symmetric lists L_1,…,L_k and every k-tuple of vertices ((u_1,j_1),…,(u_k,j_k)) with (u_t,j_t) ∈ L_t for all t, the image φ((u_1,j_1),…,(u_k,j_k)) lies in the intersection ⋂_t L_t (i.e., φ preserves symmetric lists).

Decide whether the following statement holds for every br-graph H: S_H admits a semi-conservative WNU polymorphism if and only if S_H admits a semi-conservative 3-NU polymorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem (Question 6.1) in the work "Towards a dichotomy for the switch list homomorphism problem for signed graphs" (arXiv:2104.07764). The parsed metadata indicates the equivalence has been disproved (a semi-conservative WNU does not in general imply a semi-conservative 3-NU on switching graphs), but no independent published resolution was located in the brief search.
